c74object.name: fidddle~
c74object.digest: Polyphonic pitch detector for string instruments
c74object.description: Detects up to six simultaneous pitches in a mono audio signal from a bowed or plucked string instrument (bass, cello, viola, violin or guitar profile), tracks them over time, and outputs note events as a MIDI-style list plus continuous per-voice frequency and level signals. Each sounding note holds a persistent voice slot (0 to 5) until its note-off, so the signal outlets follow a note through vibrato and glissando. Note-ons are delivered roughly 70 to 130 ms after the physical onset (the analysis window length).
c74object.discussion: Calibration: what it learns and how it helps. A profile can only guess the physical properties of your strings. The calibrate message measures them from isolated open-string notes and makes the detector use the real values. It learns three things. (1) Inharmonicity of each open string: how far its upper partials run sharp of exact multiples of the pitch. This differs from string to string, and the profile can only assume one typical value. (2) The tuning of each open string, in cents from its nominal pitch. (3) The balance of the harmonics of each string: how strong each partial is relative to the first few, for your instrument and pickup or microphone. Every string has its own balance, and the detector uses the one belonging to the string a pitch would be played on. How it helps. If a string's real inharmonicity differs from the profile's guess, its upper partials no longer line up with the model, and the detector tends to explain the left-over partials as extra notes: a single plucked note can produce a phantom copy an octave and a twelfth above it, and dense chords become less reliable. With the real values the partials line up again. In tests on synthetic strings, calibration removed the phantom notes and raised note-level accuracy on chords from 0.82 to 0.94 (F1). It matters most for plucked, stiff-stringed instruments (guitar and bass). Bowed instruments such as cello, viola and violin have very little inharmonicity, so they gain much less. Fretted notes use the inharmonicity of the string they would be played on, scaled by how much shorter the vibrating string is. Strings you did not calibrate keep the profile's defaults, so a partial calibration still helps. How to use it. Send calibrate, then pluck each open string on its own and let it ring for about a second, one string at a time and in any order. Pluck, do not bow: a bowed string is locked to an exact harmonic series, so a bowed calibration would measure no inharmonicity at all. Chords, overlapping notes and fretted notes are ignored, so only isolated open strings count. It finishes by itself when every string has been captured, or send calibrate done to use what has been captured so far. The result is stored in the calibration attribute, which is saved with the patcher, so you only need to calibrate once per instrument. Changing the profile discards it, and calibrate clear removes it. Plucked profiles. The guitar and bass profiles require a new note to start with a pluck attack: a voice that appears in a decaying ring without a fresh attack (a sympathetic string, or a ghost octave under a ringing string) is not reported, and neither are legato notes such as hammer-ons and pull-offs, which have no attack of their own. The other profiles have no such requirement.

entry.name: signal
entry.description: Outlets 0-5: frequency in Hz of voice slots 0-5 (0 when the slot is silent). Outlets 6-11: linear level of voice slots 0-5.

entry.name: list
entry.description: Outlet 12: midinote velocity slot. A velocity of 0 is a note-off. A re-attack of a ringing note sends the note-off and then the note-on.

inlet.description: Mono audio signal, ideally a close-miked or pickup signal. Also accepts the messages reset and info.

outlet.description: Frequency of voice slot 0 in Hz, 0 when silent.
Frequency of voice slot 1 in Hz, 0 when silent.
Frequency of voice slot 2 in Hz, 0 when silent.
Frequency of voice slot 3 in Hz, 0 when silent.
Frequency of voice slot 4 in Hz, 0 when silent.
Frequency of voice slot 5 in Hz, 0 when silent.
Linear level of voice slot 0, 0 when silent.
Linear level of voice slot 1, 0 when silent.
Linear level of voice slot 2, 0 when silent.
Linear level of voice slot 3, 0 when silent.
Linear level of voice slot 4, 0 when silent.
Linear level of voice slot 5, 0 when silent.
A list of three integers. Velocity 0 means note-off.

Messages in response to info (profile, calibration, analysis, timing_us, latency_ms) and calibrate progress messages (calibrate started / progress / string / complete / applied / cancelled / cleared, and calibration_data with the learned list).

method.name: reset
method.description: Discards all tracking state and rebuilds the detector with the current attribute values.

method.name: info
method.digest: Report profile, calibration, analysis settings, timing and latency
method.description: Sends from the right outlet: profile (name, voices, minfreq, maxfreq), calibration (strings captured, strings, harmonic weights learned 0/1, or none), analysis (sample rate, window size in samples and in ms), timing_us (mean and maximum analysis time per hop in microseconds, the hop budget, and the number of dropped events), and latency_ms (mean and maximum delay between the estimated physical onset and the note-on, and the number of notes measured).

method.name: calibrate
method.digest: Learn the open strings of your instrument
method.description: Starts, finishes or clears an open-string calibration. Send calibrate, then pluck each OPEN string on its own (do not bow) and let it ring for about a second, one string at a time and in any order. Anything that is not a single clean note close to an open string is ignored, so chords, overlapping notes and fretted notes contribute nothing (playing other things in between is harmless but does not help). The object measures each string's inharmonicity and tuning and the typical balance of the harmonics, applies them at once and stores them in the saved calibration attribute. It finishes by itself when every string has been captured. calibrate done uses the strings captured so far (the others keep the profile's defaults), calibrate cancel abandons the session, and calibrate clear removes the calibration. Progress is reported from the right outlet as calibrate started, calibrate progress, calibrate string, calibrate complete, calibrate applied and calibrate cancelled.

attribute.name: profile
attribute.description: Selects the instrument: 0 bass, 1 cello, 2 viola, 3 violin, 4 guitar. Sets voices, minfreq and maxfreq to that instrument's defaults and adapts the analysis window and harmonic model. The names (bass, cello, viola, violin, guitar) are also accepted. Default 1 (cello).

attribute.name: voices
attribute.description: The most notes tracked at once, 1 to 6. The profile sets this (4 for bass, cello, viola and violin, 6 for guitar). A lower value uses less CPU and gives fewer false extra notes. Setting it overrides the profile default until the profile is set again.

attribute.name: minfreq
attribute.description: The lowest fundamental frequency searched, 20 to 2000 Hz. The profile sets this (bass 28, cello 60, viola 120, violin 185, guitar 70). Lower it a little for a down-tuning. A lower value needs a longer analysis window and so adds latency: the bass profile covers a 5-string bass down to its low B (31 Hz) and uses a 372 ms window; on a 4-string bass raise minfreq to about 38 Hz to halve that.

attribute.name: maxfreq
attribute.description: The highest fundamental frequency searched, 100 to 6000 Hz. The profile sets this (bass 500, cello 1000, viola 1500, violin 2800, guitar 1400). Set it just above the highest note you play to reduce false notes. Must be at least 1.5 times minfreq.

attribute.name: calibration
attribute.description: A list of numbers produced by the calibrate message: the inharmonicity and tuning of each calibrated open string and the learned harmonic weights. It is saved with the patcher, so the calibration is restored when the patch opens; it can also be stored elsewhere and sent back. Send calibrate clear to remove it. Changing the profile discards it.

attribute.name: minlevel
attribute.description: Notes quieter than this level are ignored, -90 to -20 dBFS. Raise it to reject room noise and ringing. On the cello, viola and violin profiles a quieter note still counts when it is at least 30 dB above the noise floor. Default -58.

attribute.name: confirm
attribute.description: How many analysis frames (about 5.8 ms each at 44.1 kHz) a new pitch must persist before a note-on is sent, 2 to 24. Higher values reject short false notes but add latency. Default 6.

attribute.name: release
attribute.description: How long a note may go unsupported by the analysis before its note-off is sent, 50 to 1000 ms. Higher values bridge dropouts but delay note-offs. 0 (default) uses the profile's own value: 100 ms, or 300 ms for guitar.

attribute.name: retrigger
attribute.description: How much louder (in dB) the partials of a ringing note must become for a repeated pluck to retrigger it, 3 to 30. Lower values retrigger more easily but may split sustained notes. Default 10.
